title: Turn the Board
statement: A puzzle game stores its square board as a grid of numbers. Return the board turned 90 degrees clockwise.

answerKey.pattern: Index mapping: new[c][n − 1 − r] = old[r][c] (or transpose, then reverse each row)
keyPoints: Cell (r, c) moves to row c, column n − 1 − r
In place: transpose across the diagonal, then reverse every row
Either way each cell moves once
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(1) in place, O(n²) for a copy
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Rotate layer by layer with four-way swaps: also O(n²), easier to get wrong

hints: Track a few cells by hand: where does the top-left corner go? The top-right?
Top-left goes to top-right; in general (r, c) goes to (c, n − 1 − r).
Or: transpose, then reverse each row.
